newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines seen in the grain market on price dips.
newsitem.headline: Philippines seen in the grain market on price dips.

text.p: Philippine grains importers are expected to go back to the market on price dips next week, Manila, local traders said on Friday.
Manila grains traders said the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping had no impact on the market.

"The NFA (National Food Authority) is still negotiating for more rice imports from neighbouring countries. A Philippine company is also importing 25,000 tonnes of white corn, while another local flour miller plans to buy 25,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for March shipment," said a senior trader.

A senior official of the Philippine Agriculture Department told Reuters the NFA may negotiate for more rice from either Thailand or China. "We can entertain other suppliers, depending on their offers," the official said.
On Monday, the Agriculture official said the Philippines clinched a deal to buy up to 200,000 tonnes of rice from Vietnam.
Early this month, the Philippines bought 205,000 tonnes of Thai rice at $300 a tonne.
President Fidel Ramos has approved the import of up to 650,000 tonnes of rice to beef up the country's buffer stocks before July this year.
Philippine rice output in the third quarter has traditionally been low.
In the corn market, Philippine Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero said on Tuesday a local corn starch manufacturer is set to import 25,000 tonnes of white corn from South Africa.
Escudero told reporters the agriculture department has approved the importation at a 35 percent tariff.

The NFA said the average retail price of yellow corn increased to 10.59 pesos per kg from 10.56 pesos, while the price of white corn dropped to 10.96 pesos per kg from 11.03 pesos. The price of yellow corn at the farm level was steady at 6.82 pesos per kg while the price of white corn increased to 6.94 pesos per kg from 6.82 pesos.
Philippine wheat importers are also expected to go back in the market for U.S. wheat if prices drop to lower levels.
On Wednesday, two Philippine firms bought 35,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for March shipment through the Philippine unit of U.S. trading giant Cargill Inc, trader said.

The traders said the Philippine firms bought 8,000 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat, with 14 percent protein content, and 7,000 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat with a 13.5 percent protein content.
"Average price for both grades of wheat is more than $180 per tonne FOB," said one trader.
The two companies also bought 20,000 tonnes of western white wheat at between $156 to $158 a tonne FOB, they added.
The state agency the Department of Trade and Industry said the prevailing price of local flour remained steady, with a 25-kg of hard flour pegged at 290 pesos and soft flour at 260 pesos.
